result.summary: Bumps the minimum supported Clang compiler version from 17.0 to 19.0. It replaces the CMake feature check for aggregate CTAD with a check for C++20 CTAD on alias templates, updates CI test environments to use Clang 19, and configures clang-format to use the latest language standard.
result.problem: Supporting older Clang releases prevents developers from adopting C++20 Class Template Argument Deduction (CTAD) on alias templates and requires maintaining workarounds for older compiler bugs.
evidence: PR description: 'Most supported operating systems ship with clang-19 (or later), so bump the minimum to that and allow new code to drop workarounds for previous clang bugs. (For this bump, only C++20 CTAD will become available.)'
result.scope_notes: Touches build configuration, CI environments, clang-format settings, and documentation.
result.changed_since_previous: Removed the Xcode Command Line Tools version bump (handled separately in #36287) and updated a CI workflow runner image.
result.card: Bumps the minimum supported Clang version from 17.0 to 19.0 across CMake feature checks, CI environments, and documentation. This enables the codebase to use C++20 Class Template Argument Deduction (CTAD) on alias templates and allows future PRs to remove workarounds for older Clang bugs. Developers building with Clang older than 19.0 will be required to upgrade or use GCC.

risk.why: Incorrect compiler feature checks could prevent developers or downstreams using supported compilers from configuring or building the project.
